# B — Requirements from the build conversation and its working documents

Audit 2026-10 · compiled 2026-10-22 · read-only requirements inventory (no build status verified here — "Stated status" is what the source itself claims).

## How to read this

- One row per distinct requirement. IDs `C-0001…` are stable within this file; rows are grouped by domain.
- **Within each domain the owner-requested and assistant-promised rows from the conversation come first** (highest authority — the owner's own words, dated), then rows from the governing docs, FPBs and design boards.
- **Origin**: `Owner-requested` (Mike said it, quote + date in Source) · `Assistant-promised` (the build assistant committed to it in the conversation) · `Specified (doc)` (written as a requirement in a repo doc / FPB / CLAUDE.md) · `Designed (board)` (shown on an owner-reviewed design board in `design-studio/v2/`) · `Competitive-research rec.` (recommended from the competitor study).
- **Stated status** is copied from the source (e.g. LIVE / PARTIAL / STUB / PLANNED from `04-CAPABILITY-MAP`, "built (per assistant)" from the conversation). It is a claim, not a verification — the build-vs-requirement check is a separate audit.
- Exact duplicates were removed; near-duplicates from different sources are kept on purpose (they show the same requirement was specified, designed *and* promised).

## Sources

1. **Conversation** — session `ea84a70d…` (2026-08-09 → 2026-10-22): every owner message (68 turns incl. mid-turn messages) and every assistant commitment ("next", "wave", "I'll build", decisions with defaults). Plus `CLAUDE.md` Bank-Feed required features and business rules.
2. **docs/ia/** — `00-OWNER-DIRECTIVE`, `02-MARKET-PATTERNS`, `04-CAPABILITY-MAP` (all 346 capabilities with stated status), `05-RBAC-SPEC`, `06-EXISTING-UI-AUDIT`, `07-INTEGRATIONS-PLAN`, `08-ONBOARDING-V2-SPEC`, `09-COMPETITIVE-FEATURE-MATRIX`, `IA-SPEC` (§4 role homes, §5.6 127-widget registry, §10 waves); `PRODUCT-FEATURE-OVERVIEW.md`.
3. **FPBs** — reports-fpna, financial-reports, team-performance, nl-copilot, tenant-model-consolidation-analytics, vendor-compliance-chase, workforce-app, commissions, payroll, payments-fees, invoices, dealer-pack, bank-reconciliation, financial-control-exceptions, identity-multitenancy, onboarding; plus `COMPETITIVE-GAP-ANALYSIS-2026-10`, `ONBOARDING-VISION-AND-PLAN`, `REV-REC-WIP-SPEC`, `projects/BOOKS-PROJECTS-INTERACTION`.
4. **Design boards** `design-studio/v2/*.html` — S1–S27 (homes, review queue, access/roles, integrations hub, pay runs, receipts, receipt chase, FP&A, debt/lender, rev rec, settings), O-* (onboarding), R1/R2 (reports), F1/F2 (budget builder, FP&A analysis), V1/V2 (vendor compliance + portal), W1/W2 (Merit Workforce, expense-policy upload).

**Totals:** 5866 requirements · Specified (doc): 3952 · Designed (board): 1305 · Competitive-research rec.: 315 · Owner-requested: 189 · Assistant-promised: 105

| C-3167 | Team-performance KPI T1 Transactions categorized/approved | Def: Bank/CC feed lines this person approved; formula: `count(BT where approved_by = user AND approved_at ∈ period)` (fallback: `AL where action='bankfeed.approve' AND actor_user_id=user`); source: `BT.approved_by`, `BT.approved_at`; grain: person / entity / team / period; good direction/benchmark: Higher, but see caveat. Full-charge desk ≈ 200–600 lines/day at a clean book; fairness: Volume ≠ value. One-click batch-approving 500 ≥90%-confidence lines is trivial; hand-coding 20 ambiguous ones is the real work. NEVER rank on raw count — weight by difficulty (see composite T7) and always pair with quality (Q-family). | FPB-team-performance.md Dim 1 Family A — THROUGHPUT (volume of finished work) | Specified (doc) | computable today (Wave 1) |

Segment by `source_module` and entry complexity; do not sum raw JE counts across skill tiers. | FPB-team-performance.md Dim 1 Family A — THROUGHPUT (volume of finished work) | Specified (doc) | computable today (Wave 1) |

| C-3400 | Competitor benchmark: QuickBooks Online (+ QBO Accountant / Work) | They do: Has a "My Accountant" and QBOA Work with client/project close checklists and simple team assignment; an Audit Log of who-did-what. But no productivity analytics, no throughput/latency/quality KPIs, no leaderboard — Work tracks task status, not performance, and the audit log is forensic, not analytic.; our delta: We compute *objective performance from the ledger itself* (throughput/latency/quality/autonomy), not manual task ticks. QBO can't measure cycle-time or rework because it isn't the timestamped book of record end-to-end; we own the GL and the `action_log` spine, so our metrics are derived, not entered. | FPB-team-performance.md Dim 10 benchmark | Competitive-research rec. | — |
| C-3401 | Competitor benchmark: Karbon | They do: Best-in-class practice-management: work status, budget-vs-actual time, capacity/utilization, client assignment grid, review workflow. Strong on *time/utilization*.; our delta: Karbon measures time entered on tasks (timesheet-driven, gameable, manual). We measure finished accounting output and its quality directly from the ledger — no timesheets. We add AI-vs-human attribution and autonomy leverage (D-family), which a timesheet tool structurally cannot have. Delta: *outcome-based & AI-aware vs input/time-based.* | FPB-team-performance.md Dim 10 benchmark | Competitive-research rec. | — |
| C-3402 | Competitor benchmark: Jetpack Workflow / Financial Cents / Client Hub | They do: Recurring close checklists, deadline tracking, "who's behind," basic staff workload.; our delta: These are *checklist trackers bolted beside* the accounting system; status is manually updated (violates our "demonstrated, not asserted"). ## Owner's explicit complaints and quality bars (verbatim in spirit, dated)

These are the standards every row above is to be judged against. Quotes are Mike's own words (typos preserved where they carry meaning).

### Repo build rules that encode the same bar (CLAUDE.md)
- **Rule 3 — Completion means completion:** renders in all states, interactive elements work, real Supabase data, errors handled, design system, accessible; otherwise say exactly what is partial.
- **Rule 4 / Rule 10 — No skeletons, depth over breadth:** a page with demo arrays is a mockup; never claim built when rendering demo data; never reports without period selection.
- **Rule 2 / Rule 7 / Rule 9 — Proactive enhancement, CPA judgement, overbuild:** add period selectors, sorting, validation, drill-down unasked; build 1–2 best-in-class extras per feature.
- **Feature Audit Checklist:** every page build must cite its items in `docs/meritbooks-exhaustive-feature-audit.md` and verify each after building.
- **Design system (binding):** Merit Suite Style Guide v2.3 / `packages/merit-ui`; new or rebuilt screens must use merit-ui; no new legacy dark/emerald UI.
